newsitem.title: UK: Dixons, Kingfisher shrug off UK price move.
newsitem.headline: Dixons, Kingfisher shrug off UK price move.

text.p: Shares in Dixons Group Plc and Kingfisher Plc cruised higher on Wednesday, shrugging off a government move to increase competition in electrical retailing.
With Dixons boosted from the outset by an institutional purchase late on Tuesday of some three million shares in the retailer at 600p, the stock was up 23-1/2p or 4.1 percent at 594-1/2 by 1430 GMT.
Kingfisher also gained 23-1/2p to 702-1/2, a rise of 3.5 percent.

Analysts said the government move could in theory have a negative impact on electrical retailers but pointed out that the major chains such as Dixons and Kingfisher's Comet should be well placed in a new competitive climate.
"If you look at the retail sector in general it is the small companies that are suffering and the big companies that are doing well," said William Cullum, analyst at Paribas Capital Markets.
"It is the big companies that can bring to bear greater marketing firepower."
Analysts and dealers also said the government package had been expected and contained no fresh negative surprise for the industry.

Dealers said they were unaware of the identity of the broker or the clients involved in Tuesday's purchase of Dixons shares, which rallied sharply after results on July 9 which came in at the top end of expectations.

Dealers noted that electrical retailers were expected to benefit from continued strength in consumer spending, highlighted on Tuesday by figures for consumer credit in June which showed an increase to a record 1.28 billion stg on the month.
